name: Hydrocodone
summary: A codeine-derived opioid generally unheard of outside the United States. Generally mild in effects, used as an analgesic and cough-supressant. Sometimes used recreationally.
metabolism: Broken down in three ways: N-demethylation, O-demethylation and 6-keto reduction. CYP3A4-mediated N-demethylation to inactive norhydrocodone is the main route, with CYP2B6 and CYP2C19 contributing less. The minor breakdown product hydromorphone (less than 3% of the circulating parent drug) is formed mainly by CYP2D6-mediated O-demethylation. Hydrocodone and its breakdown products leave the body mainly through the kidneys.
saferUse: The evidence is for single-ingredient oral extended-release HYSINGLA ER tablets. Swallow whole; crushing, chewing or dissolving can release a potentially fatal dose.
Keep securely stored and out of children's reach; accidental ingestion of one dose can be fatal. Discuss access to an opioid overdose reversal agent with a clinician/caregiver.

Avoid alcohol and do not combine with benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants unless specifically managed by a clinician; profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death can result. CYP3A4 inhibitors or stopping CYP3A4 inducers can raise hydrocodone exposure and cause potentially fatal respiratory depression.
generalRisks: The boxed warning covers addiction, abuse, misuse, fatal respiratory depression, fatal accidental ingestion, alcohol/CNS-depressant combinations, and CYP3A4 interactions that can raise hydrocodone exposure. Crushing, chewing, or dissolving the tablet can release a potentially fatal dose.
